workerRuntime.assessment: Running worker launch environment has no model keys. Worker code reads DATABASE_URL from .env but does not load its other keys. Completed briefs match deterministic fallback output; model-backed worker research was not demonstrated in this local run.

independentSourceCheck.observation: Official homepage identifies an Austin digital marketing agency and Jonathan as Founder/CEO. The linked LinkedIn URL identifies Jonathan Windham. No buying interest or contact deliverability was validated.

unverified: Google OAuth consent, token exchange, actual event creation, invitation delivery, and token revocation require a connected Google account; only initiation, PKCE/state/cancellation/disconnected guards were tested live.
Verification/reset/invitation/OTP/completion email delivery was not tested; no external messages were intentionally sent.
Full model-backed Python research remains unverified in the running worker environment; API lead planning and qualification did use the configured model provider.
No browser UI, production deployment, load/concurrency/fault-injection, long-running lease expiry, or representative lead precision/recall benchmark was performed.

methodology: HTTP requests against the existing local API and shared worker. Only disposable verified identities/member fixtures were bootstrapped directly in the local database; feature records and operations used APIs. Live Tavily/model/public-registry discovery, not seeded leads. Test-only data removed afterward.

findings.title: Deep search did not yield a fully supported buyer in either SaaS cohort
findings.observed: US: 5 candidates / 0 fully supported; London: 3 / 0. Both jobs completed and their configured provider operations ran. Every London candidate lacks industry support. The quick Austin cohort produced 2 candidates / 1 fully supported.
findings.impact: A completed deep-search job is not a successful lead-generation outcome. Two deep cohorts consumed 122 reported Tavily credits without delivering a buyer backed on every requested criterion.
findings.nextStep: Improve company/industry context carried into person qualification, entity matching, and buyer-profile targeting; rerun the same cohorts before describing deep discovery as reliable. Keep unsupported candidates in Needs review.

findings.title: The running Python worker did not demonstrate model-backed research
findings.observed: The existing worker launched without DASHSCOPE_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY. Its database loader reads only DATABASE_URL from .env. Both completed briefs match the deterministic fallback text; the API, which loads .env separately, successfully used Qwen for lead planning/qualification.
findings.impact: Completed research and a ready brief do not prove that the Python model path ran. This is a finding about the tested local worker environment; production was not inspected.
findings.nextStep: Start the worker with its configured provider environment and rerun both goals. Make active model/fallback mode visible in health or job metadata. No environment or server configuration was changed in this audit.

findings.title: A FAQ question was stored and cited as factual evidence
findings.observed: Both briefs include the question “What is Jonathan Windham’s role at Blackhawk Digital Marketing?” as a key signal and talking point. It resolves to stored evidence, but it is not a factual assertion.
findings.impact: Citation integrity passes while semantic evidence quality fails. In each initial brief this was one of only two displayed key signals.
findings.nextStep: Exclude interrogative/FAQ fragments and pair answers with their questions before extraction; test this case in both fallback and model paths.

findings.title: Malformed workspace names return HTTP 500
findings.observed: Authenticated PATCH /workspace-settings with {"name":123} or {"name":{"invalid":true}} returns 500 Internal server error rather than a validation response.
findings.impact: An ordinary bad request reaches name?.trim() with a non-string value. The server stays available, but the endpoint handles typed input inconsistently with CRM DTO validation.
findings.nextStep: Validate the request with a DTO or a string type check before trimming; return HTTP 400.
